title: Who we send away
summary: The kit's D3 gate close: the honest list of who Kelwin declines, every reason visible with a better door where there is one, beside the gate line, the page's one red ask and the not-sure door — so a buyer leaves knowing which side he's on.

story: The page's conversion moment, and the end of the promise the homepage made ('…and the honest list of who we send away'). Having recognised his situation and market, the buyer now sees the four declines in plain words, then the gate that checks it both ways, the red ask, and a quiet door if he still isn't sure. The onward link asks the next question: who he'd be working with.
copy: [K] D-01 'Rent-it-forever · We’ll run it on retainer, but if nobody inside will own it, we decline.' (approved P2) · [N] Instead 'Find the owner first. Then the system has somewhere to live.'
[K] D-02 'Lead-list shopping · Renting activity is the cycle we exist to end. A list vendor is the better call.'
[K] D-03 'Pure self-serve / PLG · The system assumes a sales-carried deal.' · [N] Instead 'Different machinery, built for checkout.'
[R] D-04 'Pre-revenue · There’s no working motion to instrument yet. When the first revenue is real, come straight back.' (from the gate) · Instead 'Read the field notes meanwhile →' (/insights)
[K] 'The audit is a gate, and it works in both directions.' (homepage fit) · [R] 'Its three questions check where revenue is today, how your deals close, and what it feels like from inside.'
[R] 'Not sure which side you’re on? Talk to the team →' · [N] onward 'Who would you be working with? → About'
